title: Lee's own cipher, keyword WINCHESTER: the opening of 6 February 1813
caption: The first three cipher passages of Lee's letter of 6 February 1813 (NARA RG 59, T164 roll 3, frame 0108), with his clear words between them: "For the purposes of commerce I established with C. D. S. S. L and C. W. a cipher, a copy of which I have taken means to put in your hands". Each tile shows the figure Lee wrote and the letter of the keyword WINCHESTER it was enciphered with (19/W is figure 19 under W); the keyword starts again at W at each passage. Lee's own mistakes are marked, never silently repaired. Red tiles are wrong figures, shown as the letter the figure gives → the letter Lee meant: 24 under C gives a where p needs 13 (pur-p-oses); 17 under W gives n where c needs 7 (c-ommerce, a stray tens figure); 2 under T gives u where e needs 12 (commerc-e, a lost tens figure); and in the second passage 1 under I gives i where c needs 20 (a c-ipher). Amber tiles are slips that read correctly once followed. Lee's key slipped once: he used T twice ("16/T again"), so from "I" on every key letter is one place back; followed that way the figures give "I established". And twice his dots between figures are wrong: he wrote 12 as "1.2" (the last letter but one of established), and the two figures 1 and 1 as "11" (the h and e of cipher). The 1813 reader pencilled "purpose of commerce" and "in your hands" but could not read the rest; "I established" and "a cipher, a copy" are first read here and rest on these slips (reading_1813-02-06.md, errors.py).
key_note: Key: the keyword WINCHESTER, written by the 1813 State Department reader over Lee's figures on frame 0108. Rule: the 25-letter alphabet (I and J one letter); figure n under key letter k gives the letter n-1 places after k (1 under W is W, 2 under W is X ...). Because the key letter changes at every figure, the same figure stands for different letters: each entry here is a figure with its key letter.
